problems.problem: Rule 6 and prose: on a hard ayah the reading ends on ‘the two concerning different peoples’, an image left without its point. In the packet on 8:61 al-Tabari sets the limit himself: the truce verse concerns the Banu Qurayza, a people of Scripture with whom peace on terms of tribute is permitted, while the order to slay in 9:5 means only the Arab idol-worshippers, from whom tribute may not be accepted. The sentence drops exactly that limit, so the reader cannot tell which peoples or why.
problems.fix: Carry his limit in his own terms, e.g. “Following the command to muster force against the enemy, the Prophet is told how to answer an offer of truce; al-Tabari, on 8:61, takes it as unrepealed by At-Tawbah’s order to slay, which he confines to the Arab idol-worshippers, this verse concerning a people of Scripture.” (41 words; re-run entry-check.js.)

Rule 7 keeps the translation’s form (‘Allah’) for quotation and ‘God’ otherwise, so a reader meets both names on consecutive mornings.
problems.fix: Write ‘God’ wherever the sentence is not quoting the key verse, in quran-01-d001-p, d002-p, d005-p, d006-p, d007-p and d012-p (word counts unchanged); re-run entry-check.js on each.

problems.fix: Change ‘is announced’ to ‘are announced’ (or ‘Just after mankind is offered an exhortation and a balm for the breasts’); re-run entry-check.js.
